scenes.title: Viewing & Searching Files
scenes.narration: Data engineers constantly need to peek inside files and hunt for specific lines without opening a heavy editor.

scenes.title: Ways to Read a File
bullets: cat dumps the whole file to the screen, ideal for short files.
less pages through large files interactively without loading everything at once.
head and tail show just the first or last lines, perfect for previews and logs.
scenes.narration: How you view a file depends on its size. The cat command prints everything at once, which is fine for a small config but overwhelming for a huge log. For big files, less lets you scroll and search comfortably. And head and tail give you a quick glance at the beginning or end, which is exactly what you want when checking a data sample or a live log.

scenes.title: Searching with grep
scenes.code:
grep "ERROR" app.log        # lines containing ERROR
grep -i "error" app.log     # ignore case
grep -n "ERROR" app.log      # show line numbers
grep -r "TODO" ./src        # search recursively
scenes.narration: The grep command is your searchlight for text. Plain grep prints every line that matches your pattern, while the -i flag makes the match case-insensitive. Adding -n tags each result with its line number, and -r walks an entire directory tree so you can find a needle across many files at once.

scenes.title: Follow a Live Log
scenes.narration: Adding the -f flag to tail keeps the file open and streams new lines as they are written. This is invaluable for watching a pipeline or server in real time. When you have seen enough, Ctrl+C returns you to the prompt.

scenes.text: cat for small, less for large, head/tail for previews, and grep to find exactly what you need.
scenes.narration: Match the tool to the job: cat for tiny files, less for large ones, head and tail for quick looks, and grep whenever you need to find specific text fast.
